saints.name: Sts. Felix and Adauctus
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: A Roman priest and an unknown bystander who joined him in confessing Christ unto death…
biography: Felix was a priest of Rome martyred during the persecution of Diocletian at the beginning of the fourth century. As he was being led out to execution for refusing to sacrifice to the idols, a stranger in the crowd was so moved by his constancy that he openly declared himself a Christian.

This unknown man was seized and beheaded together with Felix, and because his name was unrecorded the Church called him Adauctus, meaning 'the added one,' since he was added to Felix in martyrdom. The two have been honored together on this day ever since.
saints.knownFor: A martyrdom shared by a priest and an unnamed convert.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain), 30 August
